fields.v: No success criterion stated by the authors for configurations (per-task success = valid + passes checks + positive NFI; comparisons with the Human Reference are descriptive). Values are means over 5 runs; NFI aspects Doc/EH/LC/CS/LP in percentage points. (1) Codex + gpt-5.3-codex: valid 99.3%, FPC 64.8%, 6.8/2.1/1.6/2.0/1.3, aggregate 12.7 (sd 0.4); 21.08 s and 4,339 tokens per successful task. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (2) Claude Code + claude-sonnet-4-6: valid 93.7%, FPC 70.0% (highest), 7.4/2.1/1.4/1.0/0.7, aggregate 13.0 (sd 0.2); 14,330 s and 50.7M tokens per repetition, 120.02 s and 424,970 tokens per successful task. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (3) Aider + gpt-4.1: valid 96.4%, FPC 66.3%, 8.1/2.3/-1.1/0.1/0.9, aggregate 13.6 (sd 0.3). Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (4) Aider + deepseek-chat: valid 73.9%, FPC 67.0%, 6.0/2.5/0.5/1.2/0.7, aggregate 11.7. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (5) Aider + gemini-2.5-flash: valid 95.8%, FPC 59.1%, 7.0/2.1/-0.5/0.6/0.7, aggregate 12.2. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (6) mini-SWE-agent + gpt-4.1: valid 98.4%, FPC 4.8%, all aspects 0.0, no successful task; 816 s and 327k tokens per repetition. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (7) mini-SWE-agent + deepseek-chat: valid 83.8%, FPC 11.5%, 2.7/1.6/2.1/1.0/0.6, aggregate 6.7; 11,780 s and 32.1M tokens per repetition. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (8) mini-SWE-agent + gemini-2.5-flash: valid 91.1%, FPC 5.3%, 0.0/0.0/0.5/0.9/0.0, aggregate 0.9. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. Human Reference: 8.0/2.0/1.1/1.5/1.5

fields.v: Tasks: 188 SWE-NFI tasks; same input to all agents (task description + code_before; code_after hidden). Configurations: 2 commercial agents with their own models, 2 open-source agents x 3 backbone models (8). Baseline: Human Reference (merged PR revision); open-source agents share models to isolate the model. Held constant: task input, evaluation suite; temperature 0 where supported. Acceptance: task-specific functional preservation checks, then rule-based NFI scoring. Repetitions: 5 per configuration and task, mean and sd reported; no statistical tests. Human intervention: none

fields.v: Highest FPC rate 70.0% (Claude Code); mini-SWE-agent configurations pass checks on only 4.8-11.5% of valid outputs. All configurations below the Human Reference on Logic Patterns (0.0-1.3 vs 1.5); several exceed it on Documentation (Aider + GPT-4.1 8.1 vs 8.0), Error Handling, Library Constraints or Coding Style. Multi-file tasks reduce Error Handling (up to 1.7 pp) and Logic Patterns (up to 1.1 pp) improvements; two mini-SWE configurations have no eligible multi-file outputs. Aggregate NFI stable across runs (sd 0.1-0.4 for Codex, Claude Code, Aider). Claude Code uses ~100x the tokens of Codex for +5.2 pp FPC; cost per successful task 120.02 s / 424,970 tokens vs Codex 21.08 s / 4,339. Differences are descriptive (no significance testing)

fields.v: Rule set cannot capture all software quality; threshold checks may miss or penalise contextually appropriate code; Python only; sparse subsets to be read with caution; stochastic agents (mitigated by 5 runs). Gaps: non-functional improvement as a distinct agent capability; logic-pattern improvement and multi-file coordination; extend to other languages and underrepresented categories; rules as feedback signals for NFI-aware agents
